name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,301

entries.clue: Checking car can go to begin with (8)

indicators.note: what comes to begin with a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: an Audi is a make of car

annotation.surface: Someone inspecting a car to see whether it can go before setting off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' and 'go' look like verbs in the surface; here 'can' is the noun, a tin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: auditing is the formal examination of accounts, a close checking of the books.

entries.clue: Release family member shortly before a politician (7)

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter
places the family member ahead of the rest

annotation.surface: A relative is let out of custody just ahead of a politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as 'soon' in the surface, but it instructs you to trim the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Removing a clamp frees whatever it gripped, so unclamping is one specific way to let go.

entries.clue: Island boy pens one epic poem (5)

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as sheep in a pen

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral; it goes inside LAD to make LIAD

annotation.surface: A boy from an island writes an epic poem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing, which suits a poem; it means encloses.
annotation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War.

entries.clue: In the afternoon, I upset mischievous child (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up-side down means read from the bottom

annotation.surface: In the afternoon, someone is annoyed by a naughty child.
annotation.walkthrough: PM then I gives PMI, which turns over to IMP. 'Upset' seems to be about feelings, but it flips the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Imp began as a small demon; it is now the everyday word for a naughty youngster.

entries.clue: Foolishly ignore old boatman? (9)

indicators.note: letters arranged foolishly are jumbled

annotation.surface: Someone unwisely brushing off an elderly boatman.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a gondolier is a specific, Venetian kind of boatman.
annotation.definitionFit: A gondolier is the boatman who rows a gondola in Venice.

entries.clue: Struggle with belief (4)

blocks.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

annotation.surface: Wrestling with one's faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word, but it supplies the W.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your view on a question is the opinion you hold about it.

entries.clue: He and Clive developed means of transport (7)

indicators.note: letters that develop change into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters; 'and' just joins the two words

annotation.surface: Two men teaming up to invent a new way of getting around.
annotation.walkthrough: A name in a clue is almost always fodder, as Clive is here.
annotation.definitionFit: Cars, buses, carts and bikes are all vehicles, the general word for things that carry people or goods.

entries.clue: Boredom that is on the rise around new northern university (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up
the reversed letters go around the rest

annotation.surface: Boredom growing at a new university in the north.
annotation.walkthrough: IE turned over gives EI, which holds NNU: E-NNU-I.
annotation.definitionFit: Ennui, borrowed from French, is the weary, listless feeling of having nothing to engage you.

entries.clue: Fanatic regularly hosting introduction to Chuck Berry (4)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every second one
a host holds a guest inside
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of FANATIC
first letter of CHUCK, placed after the first A

annotation.surface: A devoted fan has Chuck Berry, the rock-and-roll star, over as a guest.
annotation.walkthrough: Chuck Berry looks like a single name, but the clue splits it: Chuck feeds the wordplay and Berry is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Acai is a small purple berry from a South American palm.

entries.clue: Liking quiet charm (8)

annotation.surface: A fondness for understated appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: P is the musical direction piano, meaning soft; 'quiet' gives it in crosswords again and again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from French: a penchant is a strong taste or fondness for something.

entries.clue: City beach pier exposed by work (3,5)

indicators.note: stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: PIER with its first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: A seaside city's pier laid bare by construction work.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface, with beach and pier, fits the answer itself: San Diego is a coastal Californian city.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: San Diego is a large Californian port near the Mexican border.

entries.clue: Terry Jones too busy, shunning all outsiders? Wrong! (9)

indicators.note: every word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: TOO without its outer Ts and O

annotation.surface: Terry Jones of Monty Python, too busy to mix with outsiders, is told he has got it wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Terry Jones was a member of Monty Python. 'Outsiders' reads as people; here it means the outside letters of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything erroneous contains an error, so it is incorrect.

entries.clue: Murderer’s California home (4)

blocks.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

annotation.surface: The house where a killer lives in California.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis he killed his brother Abel, making him the Bible's first killer.

entries.clue: Initially pay attention after Associated Press turn up (6)

indicators.note: at the start, so take the opening letter
puts the following pieces behind AP

blocks.note: AP is the Associated Press news agency
to give ear is to pay attention

annotation.surface: A reporter urging people to listen once the news agency arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pay attention' looks like one phrase; it is split, with 'pay' giving P and 'attention' giving EAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: when guests appear they arrive or show themselves.

entries.clue: Philosopher’s calculations are the wrong way round (7)

indicators.note: the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A thinker's arithmetic has been done backwards.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is', a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Dutch Renaissance humanist thinker.

entries.clue: Son leaves cold region for European peninsula (6)

indicators.note: the letter departs from the word

blocks.note: Siberia is the cold region of northern Russia
S = son; it is removed from SIBERIA

annotation.surface: A son swaps the frozen north for the warmth of southern Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a travel story, and the swap it describes, Siberia for Iberia, is exactly the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Iberia is the old name for the landmass holding Spain and Portugal, jutting into the Atlantic.

entries.clue: Popular retail outlet coming soon (2,5)

blocks.note: a store is a retail outlet

annotation.surface: A trendy shop about to open.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward 'available in store'; the definition is the idiom, as in 'a surprise in store'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: what is in store for you lies ahead, waiting to happen.

entries.clue: Aunt cooked fish (4)

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients' form

annotation.surface: A relative prepared fish for dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'cooked' a plain kitchen verb, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: tuna is a large ocean species, sold fresh or canned.

entries.clue: American woman’s escort (5)

annotation.surface: The companion of a woman from the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Escort' reads as a noun in the surface; the answer works as verb or noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An usher shows guests to their seats, guiding them there; the verb sense fits too.

entries.clue: Wild iris can start to show flowers (8)

indicators.note: wild letters run loose into a new order
the start to a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of SHOW, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: An iris growing in the wild is beginning to bloom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Iris' and 'flowers' sit in the same garden, so the whole surface is botany.
annotation.definitionFit: Narcissi, daffodils among them, are spring flowers.

entries.clue: Worshippers spending hours in Asian river (5)

indicators.note: what is spent is used up and gone

blocks.note: Hindus worship in the Hindu faith
H = hours; it is removed from HINDUS

annotation.surface: Pilgrims whiling away hours in a sacred river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the wordplay but is a link joining it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, India and Tibet.

entries.clue: Artificial pitch that’s symbolic of Ireland (8)

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival; read 'that's symbolic of Ireland' as 'a thing symbolic of Ireland'

annotation.surface: An artificial-turf sports pitch decked out in Irish symbols.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a playing field; here it is the verb for a ship lurching, ROCK.
annotation.definitionFit: The shamrock, a three-leaved clover, is Ireland's national emblem.

entries.clue: Child of king and maid abandoned by mother (3)

indicators.note: the named letters leave the word

blocks.note: MAID without MA, a word for mother

annotation.surface: A child born to a king and a servant, left behind by its mother.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a royal scandal; 'mother' is simply MA, to be removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a kid is a young goat, and by extension any youngster.

entries.clue: Terrible fate state of mind brought about (4)

indicators.note: to bring a ship about is to turn it round

blocks.note: a mood is a state of mind

annotation.surface: A gloomy frame of mind caused a dreadful destiny.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brought about' reads as 'caused'; it means turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doom is unavoidable ruin or death awaiting someone.

entries.clue: Love god in hospital drama’s hiding ring (4)

indicators.note: what hides something holds it inside

blocks.note: ER was an American hospital drama on TV
O is ring-shaped; it goes between ER and S

annotation.surface: A romantic lead on a medical TV show is concealing an engagement ring.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's supplies a letter here, not a link: ER + S holds O.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Eros was the Greek deity of desire, Cupid to the Romans.

entries.clue: Avoid changing its speed (8)

indicators.note: the letters change into a new order

annotation.surface: Advice to a driver to avoid varying the car's pace.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as driving advice, with 'changing' a plain verb there and the anagram signal here.
annotation.definitionFit: Stepping aside dodges a blow, so to sidestep a problem is to dodge it.
